problem: The text says the firewall allows 'VPN and web into the internal LAN' and the figure shows 'allow VPN,443' to the LAN, yet two lines later it says 'The internal LAN is not directly reachable from the Internet.' A student can read this as a contradiction, and inbound TCP 443 straight to internal hosts is unusual when the chapter also says public web servers belong in the DMZ.
fix: State the purpose of the rule: the firewall allows only VPN and a single internal web portal (TCP 443) to reach the internal LAN; every other inbound connection is dropped. Public web servers stay in the DMZ. So the LAN is reachable only on those two allowed paths, never directly.
